Building, Scaling + Running Secure Agents on Kubernetes with AWS | SEPARATE REGISTRATION REQUIRED
Off-Site Location

8:30 AM – 12:30 PM

As organizations move from experimenting with AI agents to production, Kubernetes has emerged as the platform for orchestrating these workloads at scale.

This hands-on workshop explores running AI agents on Amazon EKS:
Building your EKS cluster: right-sizing for GPU workloads, selecting compute for agent execution, and designing for bursty resource profiles.

Security model for agents on EKS: trust and isolation when code generates and executes further code autonomously. How do you bound blast radius and enforce least privilege?

Using agents to manage EKS: how AI agents can operate, troubleshoot, and optimize your Kubernetes infrastructure.

Project Lightning Talk – Project Overview
Hyatt Regency | Level 4 | Regency Ballroom B-D Jorge Castro, Katherine Druckman
Project Lightning Talks
9:37 AM – 9:52 AM

Get your hiking boots ready because we are about to traverse the wild, wonderful world of the CNCF Landscape. Why you ask? We currently have more than 230 projects, and finding information about them can be a challenge. "Just go to the website" isn't enough, sometimes you need a guide to show you the ropes.

In these introductory sessions we will go over some of the diverse set of projects inside the CNCF so that you're well equipped to find what you're looking for at KubeCon.

9:54 AM
Kubernetes under Fire: Igniting Performance and Burning Through Bottlenecks with Kube-Burner
Hyatt Regency | Level 4 | Regency Ballroom B-D Andrew Collins
Project Lightning Talks kube-burner
9:54 AM – 9:59 AM

What happens when your Kubernetes cluster is pushed to its limits—does it scale or break in unexpected ways?

In this lightning talk, I’ll show how kube-burner is used to stress-test clusters, uncover performance bottlenecks, and catch regressions early.

Through quick examples, you’ll see how to run benchmarks, capture meaningful metrics, and identify issues like resource startup latencies and control plane slowdowns.

We’ll also highlight its role in upstream efforts like Kubernetes SIG KubeVirt and SIG Scalability, along with the project’s current scope and upcoming areas of development.

If you care about scalability and performance, this session gives you a fast, practical starting point.

10:01 AM
OpenChoreo: Developer Platform for Both Humans and Agents
Hyatt Regency | Level 4 | Regency Ballroom B-D Sameera Jayasoma
Project Lightning Talks OpenChoreo
10:01 AM – 10:06 AM

Kubernetes gives platform teams powerful building blocks. But turning those into a real developer experience takes months of work. OpenChoreo is a complete, open-source developer platform for Kubernetes. It's ready to use from day one, for both humans and agents.

In this lightning talk, I'll walk through how OpenChoreo provides development and platform abstractions on top of Kubernetes. It comes with a Backstage-powered developer portal, plus built-in CI/CD, GitOps, and observability. Developers can self-serve deployments without needing to be Kubernetes experts.

These same abstractions also work well for AI agents. Agents need to build, deploy, and operate workloads too, often alongside humans. I'll share what it means to design a platform that serves both audiences from the start.

10:08 AM
Architecture Without Gatekeepers: Decoupling for Neutrality
Hyatt Regency | Level 4 | Regency Ballroom B-D Kate Obiidykhata
Project Lightning Talks OpenEverest
10:08 AM – 10:13 AM

Open source only works if the community can contribute without hitting a wall. We realized our architecture at OpenEverest was unintentionally biased toward specific tools, so we rebuilt it. I’ll share how we moved to a modular plugin system that decouples our core from specific operators. By supporting everything from Valkey to competing Postgres flavors, we’ve eliminated vendor lock-in and ensured the community—not the architecture—dictates the project's future.

10:15 AM
Cloud Native MySQL
Hyatt Regency | Level 4 | Regency Ballroom B-D Matt Lord
Project Lightning Talks Vitess ↓ Slides
10:15 AM – 10:20 AM

Learn how the Vitess project and the Vitess Operator offer a k8s native solution for MySQL that offers automated high availability, self-healing & failover, integrated backups and restore, and zero-downtime updates/upgrades.

  • Slides
10:22 AM
Celebrate Flux's 10 Years!
Hyatt Regency | Level 4 | Regency Ballroom B-D Tamao Nakahara
Project Lightning Talks Flux
10:22 AM – 10:27 AM

Flux turns 10!
This talk gives an overview of GitOps and Flux (the CNCF graduated project) and why Flux has been the most trusted tool for cloud providers, small to enterprise customers, and across financial institutions to telcos.
Flux continues to push boundaries in security, scalability, and reliability:
– Security-first design including SOPS with Age post-quantum cipher, Workload Identity, verification, CoSign, and the Flux UI with RBAC, SSO, and more
– Massive scale through design, data size, and network efficiency: Kubernetes server-side apply, horizontal and vertical pod autoscaling, artifact size reduction, and multiple artifact source and data types options
– Flux’s modularity: use only needed Flux controllers, no CPU bottlenecks from app bloat, and now a Flux CLI plugin system for added capabilities
– Flux’s use of the Helm SDK for full capabilities including supporting Helm’s post-render strategies, literal mode, and more
Celebrate Flux’s 10th anniversary with us at KubeCon!

10:29 AM
Container Builds at Scale with Buildpacks
Hyatt Regency | Level 4 | Regency Ballroom B-D Joe Kutner
Project Lightning Talks Buildpacks
10:29 AM – 10:34 AM

Cloud Native Buildpacks transform your application source code into images that can run on any cloud. They enable advanced caching mechanisms that improve performance at scale. They also allow for modularity and reuse, which ensure developers across your organization aren’t wasting cycles repeating what other teams have already done.

After this short talk, you’ll be able to run buildpacks with the Pack CLI and find off-the-shelf buildpacks in the Buildpack Registry, including those from Google, Heroku, and Paketo. Finally, you’ll learn how operators of large platforms use buildpacks to make their container builds as scalable as possible.

10:36 AM
Simplifying Distributed LLM Serving: What's New in KServe
Hyatt Regency | Level 4 | Regency Ballroom B-D Gavrish Prabhu
Project Lightning Talks KServe
10:36 AM – 10:41 AM

As generative AI reshapes how organizations build and deploy intelligent applications, the demands on model serving infrastructure keep rising, teams need distributed execution, efficient autoscaling, and multi-tenant isolation, all without adding operational complexity. This session explores how KServe, a CNCF incubating project, continues evolving to meet these challenges head-on.

We're excited to walk through latest releases of KServe. These releases introduce multi-node inference without requiring a Ray head node, LeaderWorkerSet-based autoscaling for distributed workloads, and an upgrade to llm-d v0.6 for disaggregated prefill/decode serving. It also adds OpenAI Responses API routing, namespace-scoped ModelCache for multi-tenant model caching, and all the latest vLLM features, alongside meaningful security hardening across the platform.

Join us to see how KServe is simplifying production-grade LLM serving, one release at a time.

Agent Substrate: Open Layers for Agentic Systems
Salt Palace | Level 1 | Hall DE Jaana Dogan, Dmitry Berkovich, Tim Hockin, Eitan Yarmush, Luiz Scheidegger
Keynote Sessions
9:33 AM – 9:40 AM

Running agentic workloads on Kubernetes presents several challenges. Agent Substrate is a new project, built on and with Kubernetes, which enables you to securely run huge numbers of agents on Kubernetes with ultra low latency.

9:42 AM
Engineering Kubernetes for the Next Era of Workloads
Salt Palace | Level 1 | Hall DE Mike Stefaniak
Keynote Sessions Sponsored ↓ Slides
9:42 AM – 9:47 AM

AI changed what Kubernetes has to handle: container images in the tens of gigabytes, clusters approaching 100,000 nodes, and accelerators a device count can’t describe. At AWS we hit those limits early, and when we do, we fix them upstream. This keynote covers three layers. In containerd, parallel layer unpack takes the long pole out of pulling large AI images. In the control plane, we removed lock contention in the API server watch cache and the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler and fixed a scheduler hot path, all in Kubernetes 1.37. For accelerators, Dynamic Resource Allocation lets a pod ask for a GPU and network adapter on the same PCIe root, and Karpenter can now provision for it, even for nodes that don’t exist yet.

  • Slides
9:49 AM
Building the Next Generation of AI with Open Source
Salt Palace | Level 1 | Hall DE Warren Barkley, Ali Golshan
Keynote Sessions
9:49 AM – 9:56 AM

Join us to hear how NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source and working alongside the Kubernetes community to build the future of AI Factories—together. We’ll share how an open, community-driven approach is helping make accelerated computing easier to build, operate, and scale.

9:58 AM
Sandbox Your Agents
Salt Palace | Level 1 | Hall DE Jessica Forrester
Keynote Sessions Sponsored
9:58 AM – 10:03 AM

AI Agents offer unequalled automation tooling for rapid software development, but with unfettered power comes great headaches, namely how to scope and secure them in cloud native stacks. A problematic agent with too much access, either through choice or a lack of knowledge, can take down entire production stacks and wipe databases. In this talk, we explore how using core community building blocks like Confidential Containers and OpenShell, alongside emerging technology across the cloud native ecosystem, allows anyone to isolate their agentic workloads and software development processes at scale with secure, containerized sandboxes.

10:05 AM
Pods in the Wild: Reinforcement Learning on Kubernetes with OpenRL
Salt Palace | Level 1 | Hall DE Sunil Arora, Ravin Kumar
Keynote Sessions
10:05 AM – 10:13 AM

What do wild dolphins, open-weight Gemma models, and Kubernetes have in common?

Pods, of course!

By training DolphinGemma on decades of marine acoustic data, researchers are actively decoding dolphin communication. This reflects a broader industry shift: transformative AI pairs domain-specific open weights with specialized data. Far from replacing frontier models, winning architectures unite massive foundation LLMs for broad reasoning with lightweight, task-tuned models for targeted execution. While frontier models set the bar for general intelligence, the next major operational leap belongs to everyday builders: empowering practitioners to fine-tune open-weight models that outperform massive frontier baselines on domain-specific tasks at a fraction of the cost, footprint, and latency.

Historically, reinforcement learning (RL) was trapped inside elite research labs and brittle, complex runtimes. A new CNCF sandbox project, OpenRL fundamentally changes this paradigm by democratizing RL directly on Kubernetes. Now, a builder can articulate a task, point to a dataset, and use CNCF technologies to guide an open-weight model toward task mastery without requiring deep machine learning expertise.

10:15 AM
The Harness Is the New Runtime
Salt Palace | Level 1 | Hall DE Idit Levine, Keith Babo
Keynote Sessions Sponsored
10:15 AM – 10:20 AM

Agent harnesses are the dominant pattern for agentic AI on the desktop and will become the dominant runtime for agents on Kubernetes. The hard part is the move: bringing the harness onto your cluster with end user experience intact while adopting Kubernetes primitives for sandboxed execution, checkpoint/restore, scale, and security. Containers made this exact trip from developer machines to shared infrastructure in Kubernetes. In this keynote we'll present harnessed agents as your cluster's next critical workload. We'll show how harnesses combine models with a modular runtime of tools, skills, and plugins, and how leading CNCF ecosystem projects deliver the identity, policy, and observability to run them in production.

10:22 AM
One Kubernetes, Different Environments: Closing the Portability Gaps
Salt Palace | Level 1 | Hall DE Dilpreet Bindra
Keynote Sessions
10:22 AM – 10:27 AM

What does portability really mean when Kubernetes spans containers, virtual machines, and increasingly diverse infrastructure? This keynote will discuss how VM API and the Workload Conformance Working Group are tackling different sides of that challenge and building more consistent infrastructure APIs and workload expectations across the Kubernetes ecosystem.

10:29 AM
The Identity Crisis: Who is the AI Agent in Your Cluster?
Salt Palace | Level 1 | Hall DE Abdel Sghiouar
Keynote Sessions
10:29 AM – 10:39 AM

Kubernetes was designed for a predictable world. We built it to manage deterministic, stateless microservices with known communication paths, defined resource requirements, and static identity boundaries.

The rise of agentic AI completely shatters these assumptions.
An AI agent is not just another stateless workload, it is a non-deterministic entity that generates dynamic network calls, triggers external APIs, and executes machine-generated code on the fly. This behavior introduces a security blind spot: when an autonomous agent invokes a local tool or accesses a cloud database, what identity does it present?

In this keynote, Abdel Sghiouar unpacks the looming identity and resource crisis of running agents on Kubernetes. He will explore why traditional Authn/Authz and container boundaries fail when software behaves unpredictably, and showcase how emerging open-source standards are trying to redefine multi-tenancy and secure execution for the next decade of cloud-native computing.

10:41 AM
From Pod to Actuator: Physical AI and the Future of Kubernetes
Salt Palace | Level 1 | Hall DE Abhilash Somasamudramath
Keynote Sessions

Demo Theater: Agentic AI Needs Agentic Infrastructure: Autonomy on Kubernetes
Salt Palace | Level 1 | Solutions Showcase | Hall 1 | Alpine Overlook Zone | Demo Theater Yodar Shafrir
